new_statements.quote: Word stress. In general, primary stress falls on one of the last three syllables in a word. Illustrations of stress in each of these positions are provided with words from Moenat. Final stress /kaˈs̠tra/ castrà 'castrated', /bonoˈrif/ bonorìf 'early ADJ'; Penultimate stress /ɲiˈɲɔla/ gnignola 'lizard', /ˈsez̠la/ sesla 'sickle'; Antepenultimate stress /ˈfemena/ fémena 'woman', /ˈt̠s̠aneva/ ciàneva 'cellar'. [...] According to these conventions, when no accent mark is present in a polysyllabic word, stress is most often penultimate. Further research is needed to gain insight into Ladin foot structure and any categorical or gradient influences of word shape on the locus of stress assignment.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Romance-type lexical stress restricted to a three-syllable window at the right edge of the word (final, penultimate or antepenultimate); position is not predictable from the segmental string alone (orthography marks final stress on vowel-final words and often antepenultimate stress), with penultimate the most frequent pattern. The Gherdëina orthography (Forni, Istitut Ladin Micurà de Rü, 'L azënt') adds the distributional generalisation: vowel-final words mostly penultimate ('La majera pert dla paroles che tl gherdëina fina cun n vocal à l azënt tonich sun la penultima silba'), consonant-final words mostly final ('Chëles che fina cun n consonant à l azënt tonich n gran pert sun l'ultima silba'), with lexical exceptions (batum, Jevun, mefun).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing said about secondary stress in either source.
new_statements.exceptions: JIPA: vowel hiatus words like /saˈuk/ saùch carry an accent mark; accent marks also used for non-stress purposes (é vs e; Cazet pèrt). Forni (Gherdëina): some consonant-final words are not final-stressed (batum, Jevun, mefun, mesun, Sacun); verb forms with enclitics keep the base accent (SPELL 2001 p. 30).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level primary stress in citation forms; JIPA transcriptions of connected speech ('North Wind and the Sun') mark stress per word. JIPA data are from Val di Fassa varieties (Brach, Cazet, Moenat; stress examples from Moenat).
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted JIPA statement describes the Val di Fassa varieties of Ladin (Fascian: Brach, Cazet, Moenat; stress examples from Moenat) = Glottolog dialect Fassano [fass1244] under ladi1250. The supporting Forni online orthography describes Gherdëina (Val Gardena) = Gardenese [gard1241]. SPELL 2001 describes the constructed written standard 'Ladin Dolomitan/Ladin Standard'. All fall under language-level ladi1250.

sources.citation: Forni, Marco (a cura di). La ortografia Ladin Gherdëina (online orthography/grammar of Gherdëina Ladin, Istitut Ladin Micurà de Rü; linked from micura.it as 'Gramatica online (Gherdëina)'), section 'L azënt'. https://ladingherdeina.ladinternet.it/azent/L-azent.page
sources.note: Every word has a tonic accent; most vowel-final words are stressed on the penult (brama, chilo, sluseda), most consonant-final words on the final syllable (gurmel, madroz, patat), with some consonant-final exceptions not final-stressed (batum, Jevun, mefun); graphic accent mostly not written.

sources.citation: SPELL (Servisc de Planificazion y Elaborazion dl Lingaz Ladin) [E. Valentini et al.]. 2001. Gramatica dl Ladin Standard. Vich / San Martin de Tor / Bulsan. 144 pp. (Wayback copy of spell-termles.ladinia.net PDF).
sources.note: Ch. A.4 'L azent y l apostrof' pp. 28-30: purely orthographic rules (write the accent on every polysyllabic oxytone ending in a stressed vowel: starà, jené, proibì, aldò, palù; on certain verb forms; enclitics keep base accent). No statement of a default stress position.
